sentences.text: This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the first accused in Crime No.588 of 2024 of Melattoor Police Station, Malappuram,
registered for the offences punishable under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 66(D) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.

3. According to the prosecution, the accused induced the de facto complainant through social media platforms to transfer an amount of Rs. 88,000/-, out of which Rs. 20,000/- was credited to the account of the petitioner and was immediately withdrawn and thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned Counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned Public Prosecutor.
5.

The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the entire prosecution allegations are false and that petitioner has 2025:KER:73954 been wrongly arrayed as an accused and that he has no involvement in the alleged crime and, therefore, he may be granted anticipatory bail.
6. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail application.

7. The investigation conducted so far has revealed that between 12.06.2024 and 29.06.2024, an amount of Rs. 8 lakhs was credited to the account of the petitioner, which account had remained inoperative until then and continued to remain so thereafter.
It is suspected that the said amount originated from various persons, possibly cheated through cyber fraud.
8. The de facto complainant was cheated of an amount of Rs. 88,000/-, of which Rs. 20,000/- was transferred to the petitioner's account.

Since petitioner's account had suddenly become active for a period of 17 days and carried out several transactions in the meantime, I am of the view that only custodial interrogation would unravel the different aspects of the crime and also identify whether other persons are involved in this alleged offence.

sentences.text: In a recent decision in P.Krishna Mohan Reddy V. The State of Andhra Pradesh [2025 Live Law (SC) 598] the Supreme Court had observed that custodial interrogation is qualitatively more elicitation oriented than questioning a suspect who is well ensconced with a favourable order of pre-arrest bail.

entities.text: P.Krishna Mohan Reddy V. The State of Andhra Pradesh [2025 Live Law (SC) 598]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also observed that success in interrogation will elude if the suspected person knows that he is well protected and insulated by a pre-arrest bail order during the time he is interrogated.
In fact, the court went on to hold that insulating a person from arrest would make his interrogation a mere ritual.

10. Taking note of the series of frauds perpetrated on the public by various persons through cyber crimes, I am of the view that granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner would impede the course of investigation.
Hence I find no merit in this bail application.
Accordingly, this application is dismissed.

Sd/-
